test_title: PYST 30: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Desert soil is mostly found in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Desert soil** is predominantly found in Rajasthan, which houses the majority of the **Thar Desert**, also known as the Great Indian Desert.
 
• Rajasthan's desert soil is characterized by **low organic matter, sandy texture, and poor water retention capacity**.
 
• Such soil is typically formed due to **arid climatic conditions** and lacks sufficient vegetation cover.
 
• The **western parts of Rajasthan**, including districts like Jaisalmer, Barmer, and Bikaner, are most affected by desertification and have extensive coverage of desert soil.
 
• Desert soil is primarily used for growing drought-resistant crops like **millets, pulses, and mustard**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• Located in northwest India, the Thar Desert is the world's 17th largest desert and covers about **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It spans across Rajasthan and extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana.
 
• The Thar Desert plays a crucial role in shaping the soil composition of western Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Desertification:**
 
 
• Desertification refers to the process by which fertile land becomes desert, typically due to **drought, deforestation, or inappropriate agricultural practices**.
 
• Rajasthan is one of the Indian states most affected by desertification.
 
• Government initiatives like the **Desert Development Programme** aim to counter desertification in the region.
 
 
 
• **Soil Composition in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• In addition to desert soil, Rajasthan also has **alluvial soil** in regions near rivers like Chambal and **black soil** in parts of the southeastern region.
 
• Desert soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which are critical for high agricultural yield.
 
 
 
• **Climate of Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan has a predominantly **arid and semi-arid climate**, with temperatures ranging from extreme heat in summers to extreme cold in winters.
 
• Annual rainfall in desert regions of Rajasthan is generally **less than 150 mm**, contributing to the formation of desert soil.
